away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.winner: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare
matchups.recap:
Rome-ans 10:9-10 got a Guide Rec from Travis Kelce and Omarion Hampton, but the Lone Eagle spent all week bushwhacking without a compass everywhere else. Justin Jefferson turning 15 projected points into 7.0 is the kind of thing that makes you check the injury report and find nothing wrong except vibes, and Jameson Williams matched him beak for beak with a 4.3 that walked on the alpine vegetation from snap one. Ninety-two points was a ceiling this week, not a floor.

Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare read the matchup like it owed them money. Brock Purdy's 28.48 carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike, Christian McCaffrey stayed steady at 20.6, and Stefon Diggs chipped in 19.2 to make the whole thing academic by Sunday afternoon. Carnell Tate and Tucker Kraft both no-showed, but with that much firepower up top it barely registered. This one was never a tug of war — just a Pill Pusher dosing out a post hike scrub while the Lone Eagle searched for a signal.

Josh Allen went off for 40.82 and turned this into a laugher before halftime, with Tre Tucker and Sam LaPorta chipping in enough that Malik Nabers going full Dutch-oven-adjacent at 0.6 barely mattered. The Machine Knows ran this like a preseason #1 should, riding the quarterback and letting Javonte Williams' quiet 6.5 just be background noise. Boss game plan, Boss result, and honestly they could've dressed worse and still won by two scores.

Catalina Wine Mixon is stuck on the Point and Back, and the losing streak now has real legs. Trevor Lawrence's 6.16 was a Beak decision that never got fixed, DK Metcalf ghosted for 4.7, and the Buccaneers D/ST forgot to show up too. Trey McBride and De'Von Achane tried to keep the lights on but there just wasn't enough juice. Sitting under 70 points against this Machine Knows buzzsaw, it's Chief Ron Voice: "I'm disappointed in you." The Chair Force needs a new scheme before this thing spirals further.

Chef Boyardee — you'll forgive the spelling, Stefanovich, Stefanowitcz, whatever the mailman's guessing this week — put on a coaching clinic that didn't need much clinic at all. Dak Prescott went off for 29.76, Jonathan Taylor strolled for 27.2, DeVonta Smith chipped in 22.7, and the whole operation ran a pig and back from kickoff. This is the part where I'm supposed to say something measured about margins, but no — I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF, because 134.56 against this Harley Jarvis lineup was never in doubt.

Blue Ridge got a Boss night from Ja'Marr Chase (23.0) and Jalen Hurts (16.16), but everything after that was Beak on Beak. David Montgomery managed a hollow 3.4 against a 13.11 projection, and Dallas Goedert basically no-showed at 0.9. That's gonna need to patch those holes with more leaves, because this team got soaking wet everywhere but the top of the lineup. A 55.7-point beating isn't a bad week, it's a bad game plan getting fully exposed.

Little Brother had CeeDee Lamb going nuclear for 31.3 and James Cook III chipping in 20.4, and still found a way to make this a nail-biter, because Jadarian Price gave back 4.5 on a night he was priced for 12-plus, and Colston Loveland's 0.8 was like living on the Point at the tight end spot. That's the story of this team lately — flashes of Boss production surrounded by Beak decisions, and Love Thy Naber is stuck on the Point and Back after dropping their second straight.

Meanwhile Sir Jo-Nurse leaned entirely on Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 38-point eruption and Jake Ferguson's 18.3, then watched Drake Maye no-show for 8.02 and Kyle Pitts turn in a Beak 2.0, and it barely mattered. That's the whole game plan working even when half of it doesn't: know where the points are coming from, ride them, and survive the rest. Funk that Junk got the sticky buns on Sunday morning by 1.68, proof that one earthquake performance can paper over a lot of quiet holes elsewhere.

The 46er drew up a clinic this week, and Amon-Ra St. Brown made sure everyone knew it early, going off for 30.7 while Kenneth Walker III chipped in 20.8 of his own. Joe Burrow tacked on 16.18 just to make the final margin embarrassing. The Island Gudge got a Guide-Rec-caliber week from top to bottom, and 134.88 points is what a team looks like when the game plan clicks from the opening whistle.

55 Burgers, meanwhile, were Stuck in the Sewards from the jump. Jahmyr Gibbs and the Patriots D/ST did their part with 20.3 and 20.0, but Justin Herbert cratered to 7.88 on a night he was projected near 19.48, and Luther Burden III turned in a stunned little 4.7 that never threatened anything. Chuba Hubbard's 13.4 wasn't nearly enough cover. Counsel never found an answer, the deficit never closed, and a 35.9-point beatdown is the receipt for a Sunday spent completely out-schemed.

Ricky Huns is stuck on the Point and Back after a second straight loss, and honestly this one had a rotten center from the jump. Caleb Williams gave back 7.72 on a 19.42 projection, Saquon Barkley basically no-showed with 2.5, and no amount of Kyren Williams or Tee Higgins doing their part was going to cover for that. The game plan never found a counterpunch, and 71.02 points reflects a roster that spent the whole afternoon guessing.

Team Bradford, meanwhile, just let Davante Adams go supernova for 35.5 and coasted. Derrick Henry and Jordan Love chipped in Boss numbers, and even with Bijan Robinson sleepwalking to 9.6 and DJ Moore posting a corpse-like -0.1, the Campcraft Enthusiast had banked enough cushion to shrug it off. This was never competitive, more a case of one team out-scheming the other from kickoff. Team Bradford earns the Tuesday morning bragging rights outright, while Ricky Huns heads back to the drawing board still searching for a compass.

headline: Chase Brown had a bad scare survives Rome-ans by a slim margin
